allow_large: The owner added UX items to this fix on 2026-09-27
done_when: PR titles are short (a task: story title: task name; a fix: the why's first clause, 70 characters at most), a promoted spec task's ID is SPEC, the PR body labels Why and Done when and the review block opens with a plain verdict and no hash, the board's GitHub call succeeds on this repo and links each item to its PR, and forge next says which items are ready to merge with their PR link and names the findings a close stopped on; tests through the real commands prove each; the board also lists active stories first, folds finished fixes into one collapsed line with their count, and uses plainer status words; existing tests that expect the old titles, IDs, PR body or output are updated to the new wording, since that change is deliberate

findings.body: The comma in this test occurs after character 70, so replacing production's clause splitting with `why[:70]` would still pass both assertions. The other title tests use single-clause inputs. Add a `forge close` case with a short first clause followed by more text, and assert that only the first clause becomes the title. The explicit first-clause requirement currently lacks effective regression coverage.
findings.title: Not done: command-level proof that fix titles stop at the first clause

findings.body: Only the newest 25 PRs across all states receive files and checks, but downstream consumers still process the larger listing. In `src/forge/board.py:248–257`, the last 25 merged PRs are counted and missing files are treated as no Forge changes. Newer open or closed PRs therefore cause that metric to undercount. Older open PRs also lose their green-check status through `src/forge/board.py:215–223`. Fetch bounded details for the relevant PRs instead of treating omitted details as negative results.
findings.title: Fetch details for the PRs whose status and metrics are displayed

findings.body: If configured checks pass but an additional check such as `lint` fails, close rejects the PR: `src/forge/checks.py:34–50` considers additional checks too, while `src/forge/close.py:81–95` leaves the saved status as `waiting for checks`. This new path nevertheless announces readiness because `src/forge/board.py:269–274` examines only configured names. Apply the same check policy as close before instructing the owner to merge.
findings.title: Apply close's check policy before announcing readiness

findings.body: This second read uses the platform's default encoding, although `src/forge/review.py:85–91` already reads and returns the document explicitly as UTF-8. On supported Windows/Python configurations without UTF-8 mode, non-ASCII story content can corrupt the PR title or raise `UnicodeDecodeError`, stopping close before PR creation. Use the text returned by `review.task`, or specify UTF-8 explicitly.
findings.title: Reuse the UTF-8 story text when extracting the title

why: Forge's pull requests and status output bury what the owner must do: titles run to 300 characters, promoted spec tasks get 40-character IDs, PR bodies and review blocks carry hashes and jargon, the board times out on GitHub and has no links, and forge next never says what is ready to merge or why a close stopped
